The Fox News host did something unusual on Thursday night: she asked President Donald Trump a pointed question.

During an interview set to air on her show Thursday evening, Ingraham pressed the president on his Wednesday night pledge that if Republicans maintain control of the House and Senate in the midterms, he will issue $5,000 checks to every adult American citizen.

Given that many Americans are facing economic hardship because of Trump's policies, Ingraham wanted to know: Why wait?

"Why not give the money now? If you have the money, why not give it now?" she asked the president.

Trump's reasoning for delaying the payout may not assuage the concerns of skeptics who remember his other, unfulfilled promises of giving money to Americans.

"Because the Democrats can't do it. For them, it's negative growth," he said. "For us, it's very positive," Trump said. "So, we're taking in $21 trillion now. Never taken in anything close to that amount of money by any country. Four to five times more than the number two country. All because of that beautiful word that you and I both love: tariffs."

For Trump's proposed election dividend to become a reality, a lot would have to happen first.

Among them: figuring out if it's even legal because, as BBC reporter Sarah Smith pointed out, "trying to influence how people vote by making a payment is illegal."

Sending money to citizens could cost up to $1.3 trillion and would likely further fuel inflation levels — assuming Congress passes the plan.

And, yes, some find that excuse hard to swallow.
